feature: Premiere's timeline keys work the moment a recording opens
summary: Open a recording and J, K, L, I, O, M and B do what they do in Premiere straight away, with no click on the timeline first. A click on the picture still gives Photoshop's letters back to the picture tools.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default.

try.do: Open any screen recording and press L before touching anything.
Press L again for double speed, K to stop, J to play backwards, K to stop.
Press I, move the playhead with Shift and the right arrow, press O, then M.
Press B: the timeline's Blade lights. Press V to put it down.
Press P: the Pen still picks up, because the timeline has no use for P.
Click the picture, then press L: the blue ring round the timeline goes and the Line tool lights.
Click anywhere in the timeline and press L: it plays again.

evaluate: Does L playing the moment a recording opens feel like Premiere, with nothing to learn first?
When you want the Line or Measure tool on a video, is clicking the picture first (or the tool bar) a way you would find on your own?
Is the thin blue ring round the timeline enough to tell you which of the two the keys are talking to?
Does a click on the inspector or the tool bar taking the keys away from the timeline ever surprise you mid-edit?
rough: Any press outside the timeline, including the inspector and the Layers list, hands the keys to the picture, which is stricter than Premiere, where J, K and L keep working in most panels. Kept so the arrow keys and Delete still reach a list you clicked into.
The tool bar's hover tips still say Line (L), Measure (I) and so on, and on a video those letters only pick the tool after a click on the picture.
The blue ring round the timeline is not in video.html; it was added by the earlier keys task because one letter now means two things, and it is what tells you where the keys are.
A recording still opens with the Trim bar up over the picture; that is the trim task's to settle, and J, K and L work through it.
